Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

form noun

a paper to fill in

also application form, fill in a form, fill out a form

modern

M-O s.v. form (document with blanks to fill in), citing Egger

1fōrmula: long o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). The diminutive of fōrma, whose o de Vaan prints long and explains as lengthened before r and a consonant (pp. 233–234, s.v. fōrma); the diminutive has the same r and m. De Vaan leaves the derivatives unmarked.

fōrmula1, fōrmulae f.

noun, first declension

a form to fill in

Classically a set form of words: the formula of a lawsuit or a contract, and a register, as the list of Rome’s allies (in sociōrum fōrmulam referre, Liv. 43.6.10, Lewis & Short). Egger gives it the sense of a form with blanks to fill in.

Other words

  • schida fōrmulāria — a form, a printed sheet to fill in

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. form (document with blanks to fill in)

    Classically scheda or scida is a sheet of paper or papyrus (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens marks the phrase as modern.

See also form, paper, sign.

SourcesLewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: scida

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. form (document with blanks to fill in).

Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), pp. 233–234.
